newsitem.title: USA: NY Fed chief doesn't see critical reserves drop.
newsitem.headline: NY Fed chief doesn't see critical reserves drop.

text.p: New York Federal Reserve Bank President William McDonough said Thursday he does not see bank reserves falling to a point where they would impair the Federal Reserve's ability to conduct monetary policy.

Asked whether he saw reserves falling to a point where it would be difficult to conduct monetary policy, McDonough replied "no I don't, I think the main effect of sweep accounts has already been seen and it has not caused us problems in managing monetary policy."

McDonough told a conference on electronic money and banking that if banks' reserves ever got that low then the Fed might have to come up with some different methodology, for example paying interest on reserves.
He said that a Group of Ten report had concluded that the likely evolution of electronic money would not be so rapid as to have a significant effect on the ability to carry out monetary policy.

"Thus far we have always been able to figure out a way to conduct monetary policy and to be able to accomodate the creativity in the financial services sector, and I have every reason to think we will be able to do that in the future," McDonough said.
